name: PostgreSQL connection-pool exhaustion
problem: Application requests fail or stall because all database connections are occupied.
diagnostic_steps: Confirm active, idle, waiting, and maximum database connections.
Identify long-running transactions, blocked queries, and pool wait time.
Correlate connection growth with traffic, deployment, or configuration changes.
solution_steps: Reduce avoidable connection demand and restore the approved pool configuration.
Cancel only confirmed runaway or blocking sessions with database-owner approval.
Scale database or pool capacity temporarily when safe, then correct the application leak or query behaviour.
verification_steps: Connection wait time and timeout errors return to baseline.
Checkout or other affected user journeys complete successfully for the observation window.
rollback_plan: Revert pool-size or application changes if database pressure increases.
caution: Do not terminate database sessions in bulk; active transactions may be interrupted.
missing_information: Current connection count and configured limit
Recent pool or application configuration changes

name: Database replication lag
problem: Read replicas are stale or unavailable because replication is delayed or broken.
diagnostic_steps: Measure replay, receive, and write-ahead-log lag for each replica.
Check network health, disk throughput, long-running queries, and replication slots.
Determine whether stale reads are affecting customer-visible decisions.
solution_steps: Route consistency-sensitive reads to a healthy primary or replica using the approved failover process.
Resolve the resource or network bottleneck preventing WAL replay.
Rebuild a replica only after confirming retention, backups, and failover safety.
verification_steps: Replica lag remains below the agreed threshold.
Read-after-write and application consistency checks pass.
rollback_plan: Restore the previous read-routing configuration if primary load becomes unsafe.
escalation_triggers: Potential loss of WAL required for recovery
caution: Do not promote a stale replica without checking recovery point and split-brain risk.

name: Database deadlock or lock contention
problem: Transactions block or abort because sessions hold conflicting locks.
diagnostic_steps: List blockers, blocked sessions, transaction age, and affected tables.
Identify the application operation and release associated with the lock chain.
Check whether retry storms are increasing contention.
solution_steps: Stop or reduce the offending workload using the safest application control.
Cancel a confirmed blocker only with transaction-impact approval.
Fix transaction ordering, query scope, or missing indexes after service recovery.
verification_steps: Lock wait time and deadlock count return to baseline.
Affected writes succeed without retry storms.
rollback_plan: Restore prior application version or traffic policy if the mitigation worsens errors.
caution: Killing a blocker can roll back significant work and increase load.

name: Kubernetes CrashLoopBackOff
problem: One or more containers repeatedly crash and Kubernetes cannot keep the service healthy.
diagnostic_steps: Inspect pod status, previous container logs, events, and exit code.
Validate ConfigMaps, Secrets, dependencies, probes, and resource limits.
Compare the failing ReplicaSet with the last known-good deployment.
solution_steps: Correct the missing dependency, invalid configuration, or resource limit when clearly identified.
Roll back to the last known-good deployment using the approved process.
Temporarily increase healthy replica capacity only if the failing version is isolated.
verification_steps: Pods remain Ready without restarts.
Service health checks and customer requests remain successful.
rollback_plan: Undo the mitigation or restore the previous ReplicaSet if readiness declines.
caution: Repeated force deletion does not fix the underlying failure and can overload the control plane.
missing_information: Previous container logs and exit code

name: Container out-of-memory termination
problem: A container is OOMKilled because memory demand exceeds its limit or node capacity.
diagnostic_steps: Confirm OOMKilled status, memory limit, working set, and node pressure.
Compare memory usage with the previous application or model version.
Inspect heap, cache, batch, and request-size changes.
solution_steps: Roll back the memory regression when it correlates with a release.
Increase limits temporarily only when node capacity and cost controls permit.
Reduce batch size, cache footprint, model size, or concurrency as an immediate reversible mitigation.
verification_steps: No OOM terminations occur during the observation window.
Memory usage remains below the safe threshold under representative load.
rollback_plan: Restore previous limits or release if node pressure or latency worsens.
caution: Increasing limits without checking node capacity can move the outage to other workloads.
missing_information: Container limit and peak working set
Recent code, model, or traffic change

name: CPU saturation and request throttling
problem: Service latency or errors rise because CPU is saturated or containers are throttled.
diagnostic_steps: Measure CPU usage, throttling, run queue, request rate, and latency by instance.
Identify hot endpoints, loops, compression, encryption, or query work driving CPU.
Compare resource limits and autoscaling behaviour with recent traffic.
solution_steps: Scale healthy capacity or raise approved CPU limits temporarily.
Reduce expensive optional work or traffic using feature flags and rate controls.
Roll back the code path causing abnormal CPU consumption.
verification_steps: CPU throttling and latency return to baseline.
Autoscaling stabilises without an error-rate increase.
rollback_plan: Restore prior scaling or feature settings if cost or stability degrades.
caution: Scaling alone can hide an inefficient or malicious workload.

name: Disk pressure or filesystem full
problem: Writes fail or workloads become unhealthy because disk usage or inode consumption is near capacity.
diagnostic_steps: Measure filesystem, volume, inode, and write-amplification usage.
Identify the fastest-growing files, indices, logs, or temporary data.
Confirm retention policy, snapshots, and recovery requirements before deletion.
solution_steps: Free only approved disposable data such as rotated logs or caches.
Expand the volume or storage tier using the documented procedure.
Correct retention, compaction, or log-rotation settings after recovery.
verification_steps: Disk usage remains below the safety watermark.
Writes, indexing, and application health checks succeed.
rollback_plan: Restore archived data or previous retention settings if required records were affected.
caution: Never delete database, audit, or application data without owner approval and backup validation.

name: DNS resolution failure
problem: Services cannot resolve hostnames consistently or at all.
diagnostic_steps: Test resolution from affected and healthy workloads against each resolver.
Inspect DNS server health, latency, cache, throttling, and configuration.
Check recent cluster scaling, network policy, and search-domain changes.
solution_steps: Scale or restart unhealthy resolver instances using the approved process.
Roll back a faulty DNS configuration or policy change.
Reduce excessive query patterns and apply safe caching after service recovery.
verification_steps: Resolution succeeds consistently from representative workloads.
Service-to-service error rate returns to baseline.
rollback_plan: Restore the previous DNS configuration and replica count if failures worsen.
caution: Avoid hard-coding IP addresses as a permanent fix.

name: TLS certificate expiry or trust failure
problem: TLS or mTLS handshakes fail because a certificate expired, is invalid, or is not trusted.
diagnostic_steps: Identify the failing certificate, chain, expiry, subject, and trust store.
Inspect certificate automation, renewal orders, secrets, and alert history.
Determine which clients and services trust the old and new chain.
solution_steps: Renew or replace the affected certificate through the approved PKI workflow.
Distribute trust anchors and restart or reload workloads in a safe sequence.
Repair renewal and alerting automation after service recovery.
verification_steps: TLS handshakes pass from every affected client path.
Certificate expiry monitoring and automatic renewal are healthy.
rollback_plan: Restore the previous certificate and trust chain if compatibility fails and it remains valid.
escalation_triggers: Rotation cannot be completed without downtime
caution: Incorrect CA rotation sequencing can cause a wider outage.

name: Authentication service outage
problem: Users cannot sign in because the authentication service or identity provider is unavailable.
diagnostic_steps: Measure login success by client, region, and authentication flow.
Check authentication pods, load balancer health, identity provider, session store, and recent deployment.
Validate internal and external health endpoints separately.
solution_steps: Restore healthy authentication capacity or roll back the implicated change.
Fail over to an approved identity-provider path when available.
Protect existing sessions and avoid invalidating tokens unnecessarily.
verification_steps: New logins and token refreshes succeed from all supported clients.
Authentication error rate remains normal during observation.
rollback_plan: Return to the previous deployment or provider route if the mitigation fails.
escalation_triggers: All customers unable to log in
caution: Do not disable authentication or signature checks to restore availability.

name: JWT or token validation failure
problem: Valid users receive unauthorized errors because token validation, signing keys, clocks, or claims are incorrect.
diagnostic_steps: Inspect failure reason, token issuer, audience, expiry, clock skew, and key identifier.
Check JWKS availability, signing-key rotation, cache, and deployment configuration.
Compare a failing token flow with a known-good flow without exposing credentials.
solution_steps: Restore the correct issuer, audience, clock, or JWKS configuration.
Refresh cached signing keys through the approved process.
Roll back a faulty token or identity configuration change.
verification_steps: Token validation and refresh succeed for representative clients.
Unauthorized error rate returns to baseline.
rollback_plan: Restore the previous key and validation configuration if compatibility declines.
caution: Never log complete access tokens or disable signature verification.

name: Payment gateway timeout
problem: Checkout or payment authorization fails because the payment provider or integration times out.
diagnostic_steps: Measure payment success, timeout, duplicate-attempt, and provider latency rates.
Check provider status, network path, connection pools, and recent integration changes.
Confirm idempotency handling before retries or failover.
solution_steps: Reduce unsafe retries and preserve idempotency keys.
Fail over to an approved provider or queue requests when the business flow supports it.
Roll back the integration change or tune timeouts only with provider guidance.
verification_steps: Payment success returns to baseline without duplicate charges.
Reconciliation confirms no missing or duplicated transactions.
rollback_plan: Restore previous provider routing and timeout settings if errors increase.
caution: Do not replay payment requests without idempotency and reconciliation controls.

name: Webhook processing backlog
problem: Inbound provider events accumulate because webhook delivery or consumers are delayed.
diagnostic_steps: Measure oldest event age, queue depth, delivery response codes, and consumer throughput.
Check endpoint availability, signatures, event-source mappings, and dead-letter queues.
Confirm whether events are safe and idempotent to replay.
solution_steps: Restore consumer invocation or endpoint health.
Scale consumers within downstream capacity limits.
Replay failed events from the provider or queue using idempotency controls.
verification_steps: Oldest event age and queue depth trend toward zero.
Business records reconcile with provider events.
rollback_plan: Reduce consumer concurrency if downstream systems saturate.
caution: Replaying non-idempotent events can duplicate business actions.
missing_information: Oldest event age and queue depth

name: Message queue backlog or consumer lag
problem: Messages wait too long because consumers are slow, stopped, or under-provisioned.
diagnostic_steps: Measure queue depth, oldest message age, production rate, and consumption rate.
Inspect consumer health, concurrency, throttling, poison messages, and downstream limits.
Check dead-letter queues and recent deployment or quota changes.
solution_steps: Restore or scale healthy consumers within downstream capacity.
Isolate poison messages and correct retry policy.
Revert accidental concurrency or quota reductions.
verification_steps: Consumer rate exceeds producer rate until backlog clears.
Oldest message age and dead-letter volume return to normal.
rollback_plan: Reduce concurrency if downstream errors or throttling rise.
caution: Scaling consumers can overload downstream databases or providers.

name: Redis or cache outage
problem: Requests fail or slow down because the cache is unavailable, evicting heavily, or serving invalid data.
diagnostic_steps: Check cache node health, memory, evictions, connections, replication, and latency.
Determine whether the cache holds sessions, locks, rate limits, or disposable data.
Measure database and dependency load caused by cache misses.
solution_steps: Fail over to a healthy replica or restore cache capacity using the approved process.
Apply controlled bypass only for data safe to recompute.
Correct memory policy, key growth, or connection configuration after recovery.
verification_steps: Cache latency, hit rate, and connection errors return to baseline.
Downstream systems remain healthy as cache traffic recovers.
rollback_plan: Remove bypass and restore previous routing if downstream load increases.
caution: Flushing a cache can cause data loss, logout storms, or downstream overload.

name: API rate-limit or WAF misconfiguration
problem: Legitimate traffic is blocked by an incorrect throttling or firewall rule.
diagnostic_steps: Measure rejected traffic by rule, client, route, account, and geography.
Compare the active edge policy with the previous approved version.
Confirm whether the traffic is legitimate and whether an attack is also present.
solution_steps: Disable or narrow only the identified faulty rule with security approval.
Apply account, token, or route-aware limits instead of broad shared-IP blocking.
Roll back the edge-policy deployment when safe.
verification_steps: Legitimate success rate returns without a security-event increase.
Rate-limit metrics match the intended customer policy.
rollback_plan: Restore the previous policy immediately if attack traffic or abuse increases.
caution: Do not disable the entire WAF or rate-limiting layer.

name: Load balancer has no healthy upstream
problem: External traffic receives gateway errors because the load balancer sees no healthy backend.
diagnostic_steps: Inspect target health, health-check path, ports, security groups, and backend readiness.
Compare internal service health with load-balancer observations.
Review deployment, certificate, network, and health-check configuration changes.
solution_steps: Restore healthy backends or correct the health-check configuration.
Shift traffic to a healthy region, target group, or prior deployment when approved.
Remove unhealthy targets only after preserving sufficient capacity.
verification_steps: Targets remain healthy and gateway errors return to baseline.
External and internal synthetic tests both pass.
rollback_plan: Return traffic to the prior target group or configuration if errors worsen.
escalation_triggers: Health checks pass internally but fail externally
caution: Do not mark unhealthy targets healthy by weakening checks without understanding the failure.

name: Application deployment regression
problem: Errors or latency begin immediately after a new application release.
diagnostic_steps: Correlate error and latency changes with the release timestamp and affected cohort.
Compare logs, metrics, feature flags, schema, and configuration between versions.
Confirm rollback and database compatibility.
solution_steps: Pause further rollout and roll back to the last known-good version when safe.
Disable the implicated feature flag or code path as a reversible mitigation.
Preserve diagnostics and open a defect with the exact regression evidence.
verification_steps: Error rate and business metrics return to the pre-release baseline.
The prior version remains stable during the observation window.
rollback_plan: Reapply the new version only after the regression is understood and validated.
caution: Confirm backward compatibility before rolling back migrations or stateful services.
missing_information: Metric comparison before and after release

name: Invalid configuration, secret, or feature flag
problem: A service fails because a runtime configuration, secret, endpoint, or feature flag is incorrect.
diagnostic_steps: Compare the active configuration and secret references with the last known-good version.
Check secret expiry, permissions, mount status, and configuration rollout events.
Identify whether only new pods or all instances are affected.
solution_steps: Restore the last known-good configuration or secret version.
Roll back the feature flag or configuration deployment.
Restart or reload only the workloads that require the corrected values.
verification_steps: New and existing instances pass configuration and dependency checks.
Authentication, startup, and affected requests remain healthy.
rollback_plan: Restore the previous configuration version if the correction causes new failures.
caution: Do not expose secret values in logs, tickets, or AI prompts.

name: Third-party dependency outage
problem: A critical external provider is degraded or unavailable.
diagnostic_steps: Confirm provider status, request failures, latency, regions, and affected operations.
Check credentials, quotas, DNS, and recent integration changes to rule out local causes.
Determine available fallback, queueing, and graceful-degradation paths.
solution_steps: Activate the approved fallback provider or degraded mode.
Queue safe operations for later processing and communicate limitations.
Reduce retry storms and follow the vendor escalation process.
verification_steps: Provider or fallback success rate returns to the target.
Queued operations reconcile after recovery.
rollback_plan: Return to primary provider gradually and remove degraded mode after validation.
caution: Uncontrolled retries can amplify both your outage and the provider outage.

name: Network packet loss or connectivity degradation
problem: Requests intermittently fail or slow because packets are dropped or routes are unstable.
diagnostic_steps: Measure packet loss, retransmissions, latency, and path changes from affected locations.
Compare zones, nodes, subnets, and healthy control paths.
Inspect network-device, cloud, and policy changes.
solution_steps: Reroute traffic away from the affected path or zone.
Roll back the network or policy change when identified.
Reduce cross-zone dependency until connectivity stabilises.
verification_steps: Packet loss and retransmissions return to normal.
Application success and latency recover across affected locations.
rollback_plan: Restore prior routing if the alternate path is unstable or saturated.
caution: Avoid broad firewall changes that weaken security.

name: Object storage access failure
problem: Applications cannot read or write files because object storage is unavailable or access is denied.
diagnostic_steps: Check provider status, bucket policy, credentials, endpoint, DNS, quota, and region.
Separate access-denied failures from timeouts and missing-object errors.
Confirm whether temporary upload, download, or permanent data paths are affected.
solution_steps: Restore the correct scoped credentials or bucket policy.
Use an approved alternate region or temporary storage path when data classification permits.
Queue non-critical writes for retry with bounded backoff.
verification_steps: Representative uploads and downloads pass with least-privilege access.
No unauthorised public exposure is introduced.
rollback_plan: Restore previous policy or endpoint if access or security worsens.
caution: Never make a private bucket public as an availability workaround.

name: CDN outage or stale-cache incident
problem: Users receive stale, missing, or failed content because CDN caching or origin routing is incorrect.
diagnostic_steps: Compare CDN and direct-origin responses by region and cache status.
Inspect cache keys, TTL, purge status, origin health, and edge rules.
Identify whether content correctness or only performance is affected.
solution_steps: Purge only the affected cache keys or roll back the faulty edge rule.
Bypass the CDN for a narrow route when origin capacity is safe.
Correct cache headers and keys after recovery.
verification_steps: Content and status codes are correct across representative regions.
Origin load remains within safe limits.
rollback_plan: Restore previous caching rules if origin load or errors increase.
caution: A broad purge or bypass can overload the origin.

name: Email or notification delivery delay
problem: Transactional messages are delayed or missing because provider, queue, template, or consumer processing is unhealthy.
diagnostic_steps: Measure queue age, provider acceptance, bounce, rejection, and consumer rate.
Check templates, suppression lists, credentials, quotas, and provider status.
Separate delayed delivery from failed generation.
solution_steps: Restore consumers or provider credentials and scale within provider limits.
Fail over to an approved channel for critical notifications.
Replay safe messages with deduplication controls.
verification_steps: Queue age falls and representative messages are delivered.
Duplicate and bounce rates remain within limits.
rollback_plan: Reduce replay or concurrency if duplicates or provider throttling increases.
caution: Bulk replay can send duplicate or outdated customer messages.

name: Data corruption or integrity mismatch
problem: Stored or processed data is inconsistent, missing, duplicated, or corrupted.
diagnostic_steps: Stop or isolate the suspected writer and preserve evidence.
Identify affected records, time window, source of truth, and last verified backup.
Compare checksums, audit events, and reconciliation results.
solution_steps: Prevent further writes through the narrowest safe control.
Restore or repair data only from a verified source with owner approval.
Reconcile downstream systems and document every correction.
verification_steps: Checksums, invariants, and business reconciliation pass.
No new inconsistent records appear during observation.
rollback_plan: Retain snapshots and provide a reversible correction plan before modifying production data.
caution: Do not run ad-hoc production updates before preserving evidence and validating backups.

name: Credential or secret exposure
problem: An API key, token, password, or private key may have been exposed.
diagnostic_steps: Determine the secret type, scope, exposure location, and first possible exposure time.
Review access logs for suspicious use without copying the secret.
Identify every system and integration that trusts the credential.
solution_steps: Revoke and rotate the credential through the approved emergency process.
Remove the exposed value from active logs, repositories, and caches where feasible.
Update dependent systems and increase monitoring for abuse.
verification_steps: Old credential is rejected and new credential works only where intended.
No continuing unauthorised use is detected.
rollback_plan: Maintain a coordinated cutover plan; do not reactivate the exposed credential.
caution: Do not paste exposed secrets into tickets, chat, logs, or AI prompts.

name: DDoS or abusive traffic spike
problem: Service capacity is consumed by malicious or abnormal traffic.
diagnostic_steps: Measure traffic rate, source distribution, routes, user agents, and error patterns.
Separate legitimate demand from abusive traffic.
Inspect CDN, WAF, load balancer, and infrastructure saturation.
solution_steps: Enable approved DDoS protections and narrow rate controls.
Challenge or block malicious patterns without broad customer impact.
Scale protected capacity only where it does not amplify cost risk.
verification_steps: Legitimate success rate recovers while abusive traffic is mitigated.
Infrastructure utilisation returns to safe levels.
rollback_plan: Remove emergency blocks gradually after traffic normalises and false positives are reviewed.
caution: Overly broad IP blocks can deny service to legitimate shared networks.

name: Logging or observability pipeline failure
problem: Logs, metrics, or traces are unavailable, delayed, or incomplete during an incident.
diagnostic_steps: Check collector, queue, processor, storage, and query-layer health.
Measure ingestion lag, dropped events, disk pressure, and backpressure.
Confirm application health independently because observability may be wrong.
solution_steps: Restore capacity or clear approved backpressure points.
Reduce non-essential telemetry volume temporarily.
Correct retention, quota, or pipeline configuration.
verification_steps: Ingestion lag returns to normal and recent telemetry is queryable.
No critical audit or security events are missing.
rollback_plan: Restore prior sampling and retention after pipeline stability is confirmed.
caution: Do not delete required audit or security logs to restore capacity.

name: Scheduled job or cron failure
problem: A scheduled task did not run, ran late, or repeatedly failed.
diagnostic_steps: Check scheduler history, next run, locks, credentials, and execution logs.
Determine business impact and whether rerun is idempotent.
Inspect recent schedule, timezone, deployment, and permission changes.
solution_steps: Correct the schedule, lock, credential, or runtime failure.
Run the job manually only after confirming idempotency and downstream capacity.
Add missed-run and duration alerts.
verification_steps: The job completes once and the next scheduled run is correct.
Business output reconciles without duplicates.
rollback_plan: Stop a manual rerun if duplicates or downstream pressure appear.
caution: Manual reruns can duplicate transactions or notifications.

name: Unknown or insufficiently observed incident
problem: The incident does not match a known case or lacks enough evidence for a specific remediation.
diagnostic_steps: Establish incident owner, scope, start time, and customer impact.
Collect errors, logs, traces, metrics, dependencies, and recent changes.
Create and test reversible hypotheses one at a time.
solution_steps: Stabilise through the safest documented generic mitigation.
Escalate to the service owner when confidence remains low.
Avoid irreversible actions until evidence supports them.
verification_steps: The affected user journey and system health indicators recover.
The confirmed cause and effective action are documented for a new runbook case.
rollback_plan: Stop any mitigation that worsens impact and restore the last known-good state.
caution: Generic advice must not be treated as permission for destructive actions.
